fix: Use the fallible constructor so out-of-range finite values (e.g. INCULAR_MEMORY_LOG=1e300) disable the log instead of panicking: `Duration::try_from_secs_f64(seconds).ok().filter(|interval| !interval.is_zero())` (Duration::try_from_secs_f64 is stable since 1.66) and drop the is_finite/> 0 check.

evidence:
let alive: Vec<([f32; 4], f32)> = flashes
    .values()
    .filter_map(|flash| Some((flash.bounds, fade(flash.started[index])?)))
fix: paint_flashes runs on every painted frame while a flash option is enabled and allocates a new Vec per enabled phase. Keep a scratch field `flash_scratch: Vec<([f32; 4], f32)>` on the runner, `clear()` it at the start of each phase and push into it (capacity is kept across frames). This needs `&mut self` on paint_flashes and paint_overlay; if the caller only holds `&self`, put the scratch behind a RefCell.

Make tree_nodes consume its input: `fn tree_nodes(deltas: Vec<TreeDelta>) -> HashMap<DevWidgetId, WidgetNode>`, pre-sized with `HashMap::with_capacity`, and move `*root` and the `rest` nodes out of each Snapshot delta. The 4 Hz sampler at line 944 then passes `snapshot` by value with no per-node clone of a whole tree. The GetWidgetTree call site (line 278, outside this range) passes `deltas.clone()` because the response still needs `deltas`.

hovered is cleared a few lines later, so the clone (one PathBuf allocation per hovered file) is wasted: `let mut files = std::mem::take(&mut self.hovered);` and delete the later `self.hovered.clear();`.

Both parameters are only read: `monitors` is used only as `&monitors` and `primary` only through `.as_ref()`. Change to `monitors: &[MonitorHandle], primary: Option<&MonitorHandle>` and drop the `.as_ref()` at line 32; callers pass `&monitors` and `primary.as_ref()`.
DisplayId values are unique by construction (index plus generation), so stability is irrelevant: `snapshots.sort_unstable_by_key(|display| display.id);`.
